title: Probing LLMs for hate speech detection: strengths and vulnerabilities

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating zero-shot classification performance on hate speech datasets and using LDA-based topic modeling on the errors to reveal model vulnerabilities, such as false positives triggered by sensitive racial terms (e.g., misclassifying neutral statements about black or white communities as hateful).

Analyzing misclassifications in hate speech detection to identify instances where the model either flags neutral discussions as toxic or fails to recognize hateful intent due to an inability to parse polysemous slang terms related to sexual orientation (e.g., 'dyke', 'gay').

Conducting an error analysis on the ToxicSpans dataset using topic modeling to demonstrate that models frequently and incorrectly misclassify standard ideological posts, political discourse, and fact-checking news statements as toxic.

Evaluating model performance using the HateXplain dataset, which explicitly annotates hate speech directed at religious groups, and analyzing misclassifications involving religious identifiers in the prompt's target community variables.
